newsitem.title: USA: Clinton lead edges to 8.5 percent in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton lead edges to 8.5 percent in Reuters poll.

text.p: President Bill Clinton edged up slightly to an 8.5 percentage point lead -- from 8.1 points on Wednesday -- over Republican Bob Dole in the latest Reuters tracking poll released on Thursday.
Clinton had 44.2 percent in the new daily survey, Dole had 35.7 percent and Reform Party candidate Ross Perot 6.1 percent, with others and undecided making up the rest.

The poll conducted by John Zogby Group International for Reuters is a survey of about 900 likely voters over a three day period producing a three-day rolling average. It has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percentage points. This poll covered Monday through Wednesday.
In the earlier poll released on Wednesday, Clinton had 44.7 percent, Dole 36.6 percent and Perot 4.4 percent.
"All trends remain basically the same as Clinton continues to lead among all age groups, every region except the South, among Roman Catholics, women and minorities," said pollster John Zogby.
Dole and Clinton "are in a dead heat in the South among white voters, those earning $75,000 or more and among men," Zogby said.
In the latest poll about 48 percent felt that Clinton deserved re-election while 41 percent disagreed.
If the election for president were held today, for whom would you vote, Clinton, Dole, or Perot?
